question: The asthenosphere is the extremely viscous, mechanically weak, and ductile-deformable region of the upper ______ of the Earth.
solution:
The correct answer is __**mantle**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The asthenosphere is the extremely viscous, mechanically weak, and ductile-deformable region of the upper **mantle** of the Earth.
 
• It lies below the lithosphere, which includes the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle.
 
• The asthenosphere is critical for plate tectonics because it allows the rigid lithospheric plates to move on top of it.
 
• It is composed of partially molten rock that flows very slowly, which facilitates the movement of tectonic plates.
 
• This layer is located approximately 100 to 200 kilometers below the Earth's surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of the asthenosphere was first proposed by the American geologist Joseph Barrell in 1914.
 
• The term "asthenosphere" comes from the Greek word "asthenes," meaning weak, indicating its mechanically weak nature.
 
• The temperature in the asthenosphere ranges from approximately 1,300 to 2,500 degrees Celsius.
 
• Seismic waves travel more slowly through the asthenosphere than through the lithosphere, indicating its partially molten state.
 
• Understanding the properties and behavior of the asthenosphere is essential for studying geological phenomena such as earthquakes, volcanic activity, and mountain building.
